questions.question: How do scientists decide how to group organisms into smaller sub-groups within larger ones?
options: By looking at similarities and differences in their physical and genetic features
By sorting them alphabetically by their common names
By grouping them solely by where they live in the world
By the order in which they were first discovered

questions.question: What is the correct hierarchy of groups used by scientists to classify organisms, from the largest to the smallest?
options: Kingdom down to species
Species up to kingdom
Phylum down to genus
Family up to order

questions.question: Which of the following is true about larger classification groups, such as kingdoms, compared to smaller groups like species?
options: They contain fewer organisms with more similarities in their features
They contain more organisms with fewer similarities in their features
They contain only organisms that look identical to one another
They contain organisms that can all interbreed to produce fertile offspring

questions.question: What biological definition describes a group of organisms belonging to the same species?
options: A group of individuals with similar features and genes that can reproduce to make fertile offspring
A group of organisms that share the exact same habitat and eat the same food
A collection of organisms that look identical but cannot breed with one another
A group of animals that live in the same geographic region and have the same life span

questions.question: What do the two parts of a species' binomial scientific name represent?
options: The kingdom and the phylum
The family and the order
The genus and the species
The class and the family

questions.question: Besides observable macroscopic features like body shape, what other level of characteristics do scientists use to classify organisms?
options: The size of their ecological footprint on land
Their characteristics at the microscopic, cellular level
The speed at which they can run, swim, or fly
Their behavioral preference for day or night activity

questions.question: Which of these is a key cellular difference used to distinguish and group animals, plants, fungi, and bacteria?
options: The presence of mitochondria in all bacterial cells
The presence or absence of a cell wall and a nucleus
The colour of the cytoplasm under a magnifying glass
The total number of proteins in the cell membrane

questions.question: If an organism's cells contain chloroplasts and cellulose cell walls, into which kingdom would it be classified?
options: Animals
Fungi
Plants
Bacteria

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of using a classification key in biology?
options: To calculate the exact population size of an endangered species
To find out which groups organisms are classified into
To measure the physical growth rate of a plant over time
To clone an organism in a laboratory setting

questions.question: What does a classification key consist of to help identify an unknown organism?
options: A series of questions about the features of organisms
A list of all historical scientists who studied the organism
A set of chemical formulas representing cellular respiration
A map showing global migration patterns of animals

questions.question: Why is biological classification so useful to scientists?
options: It helps us organise and make sense of biodiversity
It allows us to predict the weather patterns of different biomes
It prevents new species from evolving in the wild
It reduces the number of species that need to be protected

questions.question: When conducting fieldwork, what is a key task that scientists must do to study local biodiversity?
options: Take wild organisms back to keep as domestic pets
Make, record and interpret observations of organisms in the field
Change the physical habitat to make it easier to see animals
Keep all findings secret from other researchers

questions.question: How can a researcher quickly identify and classify an unknown insect while working directly in its natural habitat?
options: By guessing its name based on its colour
By using a classification key in the field
By sequencing its entire genome on-site without tools
By waiting to see if it mates with a known species

questions.question: Which practice demonstrates working safely in the field while minimising harm to living organisms?
options: Leaving rubbish behind to provide shelter for small insects
Carefully returning turned-over rocks to their original positions
Collecting as many live specimens as possible to store in plastic bags
Clearing away all plants in an area to get a clearer view of the soil

questions.question: If two organisms mate but their offspring is sterile (incapable of reproducing), what does this tell us?
options: The parents belong to different species
The parents belong to different kingdoms
The parents do not have any cell walls
The parents did not share a common habitat

questions.question: An organism is multicellular, has cell walls made of chitin, but lacks chloroplasts. Which kingdom does it belong to?
options: Animals
Plants
Fungi
Bacteria
